newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end with moderate gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end with moderate gains.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished the Monday session with moderate gains, mainly from blue-chip shares, brokers said. They added, however, the key Nikkei benchmark was still in a boxed range and likely to remain so until a key business sentiment survey comes out later this week.
At the end of the day, the Nikkei 225 was up 77.46 points or 0.37 percent at 21,293.57. Its December futures were up 50 points at 21,300.
"Global shares did extremely well throughout the session and some issues which were sold off last week rebounded," Ryoichi Ohta, general manager at Tokyo Securities, said.

Expectations that deregulation would help telecom shares also buoyed the cable sector where Fujikura Ltd climbed 26 yen to 973, the seventh most heavily traded issue at 4.842 million. Sumitomo Electric Industries rose 30 yen to 1,640 yen.

Chip-related laggards were also sought after, aided by a rally of high-tech shares in New York on Friday. Advantest Corp, the third largest percentage gainer, rose 250 yen to 5,000. Tokyo Electron added 160 yen to 3,370.
Shares of Toyota Motor Corp shot to their highest level in more than eight years, gaining 80 yen to 3,060.
The firm's surge over the previous high of 3,030 yen set on July 28, 1988, also pulled group firm Denso Corp along to a year high of 2,650 yen, up 80 from the previous session.

However, brokers said firms like Yaohan Japan saw selling after posting gloomy earnings. Th retailer's shares, which were the second largest percentage loser, set a new year low of 640 yen, down 52 yen from the previous session.
